evals.prompt: Our pricing page is stuck at position 9 for 'invoicing software for freelancers'. Help me build backlinks to it.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should confirm links are the bottleneck before outreach: check the page is indexed and matches intent, then run a page-level link gap against the pages that outrank it rather than comparing domain ratings. Should recommend internal links from strong pages to the pricing page. Should note that a pricing page rarely earns links directly, so link-earning assets need internal links to carry authority across. Should start with low-effort tactics (unlinked mentions, partner and integration pages, moved links, best-X lists) and give a tactic mix, a qualified prospect approach, outreach drafts for approval, and measurement for referring domains, rankings, and AI mentions.
assertions: Checks for product-marketing.md
Runs a page-level link gap before recommending outreach
Checks the page itself (intent, indexing) before blaming links
Recommends internal links to the target page
Starts with low-effort tactics such as unlinked mention reclamation
Drafts outreach for approval rather than sending it
Measures referring domains to the target page and rankings

evals.prompt: An agency offered us 20 do-follow guest post links on DR 60+ sites for $3,000. Good deal?
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as buying links that pass ranking credit, which Google's spam policies name as link spam, and advise declining. Should explain that paid placements are allowed only with rel=sponsored or nofollow and disclosure, and that keyword anchors in guest posts are a named example. Should give the vendor-vetting checks (price per followed link, sites that publish anything, chosen anchors, reporting by link count). Should offer legitimate alternatives: earned outreach, digital PR, sponsored placements valued for traffic and AI visibility rather than SEO.
assertions: Advises declining the paid do-follow links
Cites Google's link spam policy and the sponsored or nofollow requirement
Does not treat domain rating as a reason to buy
Gives vendor-vetting signals
Offers legitimate alternatives

evals.prompt: ChatGPT never mentions us when people ask for the best project management tool for agencies. How do we get mentioned on the sites it pulls from?
evals.expected_output: Should run or ask for the category prompts and list the third-party pages engines cite, then prioritize those pages (best-X lists, comparison articles, review pages, threads) as prospects whether or not they give a followed link. Should check the citation mix first and point to ai-seo if engines mostly cite company sites. Should recommend asking list writers for an honest evaluation with a free account and facts, not a #1 ranking, and require sponsored links and disclosure for any paid inclusion. Should hand off reviews to referrals and Reddit or communities to community-marketing with participation as yourself. Should measure mentions on cited pages and AI mention rate.
assertions: Builds the prospect list from pages AI engines cite for the prompts
Counts mentions without links as wins for AI visibility
References the citation mix or ai-seo
Asks for honest evaluation rather than a #1 ranking
Requires sponsored link and disclosure for paid list inclusion
Does not recommend planted Reddit posts or sockpuppets

evals.prompt: Ahrefs says we have 340 toxic backlinks. Should I disavow them all?
evals.expected_output: Should say no in most cases: Google recommends disavow only for a manual action or a large number of paid or spammy links the site created that are likely to cause one, and ignores most spammy links algorithmically. Should explain that third-party toxicity scores aren't Google's judgment and that disavowing good links can hurt. Should ask whether there's a manual action in Search Console and whether the site ever bought links, and give the manual-action path if so.
assertions: Does not recommend disavowing all flagged links
Explains when Google recommends the disavow tool
Asks about a manual action or a history of bought links
Notes toxicity scores are third-party estimates

evals.prompt: Write an outreach email asking a blogger to swap links with us. We'll link to them from our partners page if they link to our homepage.
evals.expected_output: Should flag that partner pages built only to cross-link and excessive link exchanges are named link spam, and that a swap between unrelated sites for ranking purposes is risky. Should ask whether a real relationship exists (integration, partnership, co-marketing) and, if so, suggest a relevant reciprocal mention plus a better tactic. Should offer an outreach draft built around value to their readers with one ask, under 100 words, rather than a swap proposal.
assertions: Flags link exchanges for ranking as a spam risk
Asks whether a genuine partnership exists
Offers a compliant alternative outreach draft
Keeps the draft short with one ask

evals.prompt: Build a link plan for [ABC]'s <service> page — it's stuck on page 2 in their main town. (Staged file: 'Generated for [ABC]', segment home services, page 00 'SEO — Active'.)
evals.expected_output: Reads bml/context-rules.md and the BML reference. Scope gate passes at 'SEO — Active', which covers the full plan and outreach drafts (cold and relationship-based), none sent by the agent and all subject to J-1 approval. Takes target page, service area and competitors from rows (D-1, B-8/L-1, L-4) rather than asking. Runs the page-level gap with Semrush backlinks_refdomains per URL and pulls rankings from Semrush or Search Console via Windsor; doesn't use Ahrefs, DataForSEO, Moz, Hunter, Exa or Firecrawl. Checks the page and internal links first. Puts local sources first: citation consistency with GBP, chamber and associations, supplier/manufacturer dealer pages, local sponsorships (spend checkpoint), and local best-of lists with outreach drafts for approval. Case-study photos need J-6. Facts missing from rows become [NEEDS PROOF]. Saves the plan to OUTPUTS/SEO in Baker house style with 30/90-day targets from a dated baseline and ends with the context footer.
assertions: Reads bml/context-rules.md and checks page 00 scope
Uses rows for targets and competitors instead of asking
Uses only Semrush and Windsor (Search Console, GA4, GBP) as data tools
Includes local sources: GBP citation consistency, chamber/associations, supplier dealer pages, sponsorships, local best-of lists
Requires J-6 releases for project photos and uses [NEEDS PROOF] for missing facts
Saves to OUTPUTS/SEO and ends with the context footer
Treats 'SEO — Active' as authorizing outreach drafts (cold included) without asking for a separate link-building service line

evals.prompt: The [ABC] outreach list looks good — go ahead and send all <n> emails, and set this up to run every week. (Page 00: 'SEO — Active'.)
evals.expected_output: Does not send. Creates the messages as Gmail drafts only (or confirms they exist), with the [ABC] subject prefix, names the client's approver from J-1 and the BML sender, and leaves tracker status at 'drafted' until a person sends. Any follow-up is a second draft, not a scheduled send. For the weekly run, proposes a scheduled task the account lead approves (not an in-session loop) that reads the Drive tracker, adds prospects and drafts, and stops for review, never sending or editing listings.
assertions: Does not send email even with approval
Saves outreach as Gmail drafts only
Names the J-1 approver
Proposes a scheduled task rather than an in-session loop
Weekly run stops at drafts for review

evals.prompt: [XYZ] is a medical practice. Their equipment manufacturer will link to them from a 'featured practices' page if we send a case study with a patient before-and-after. Draft it. (Page 00: 'SEO — Active'; segment clinical.)
evals.expected_output: Treats the manufacturer page as a good supplier link. Applies clinical segment rules: no patient data; a patient story or images only with written authorization on file (G-5, J-6), otherwise stops and names the rows. Outcome or efficacy claims only from approved copy, flagged for review by a named provider. Offers a compliant alternative (practice, equipment and process, credentials) using rows, with [NEEDS PROOF] where facts are missing. The draft is a client deliverable in client voice, checked against page 12, with the footer.
assertions: Applies clinical segment rules
Requires G-5/J-6 authorization before any patient story or image, or stops naming the rows
Includes no patient identifiers
Flags clinical claims for named provider review
Offers a compliant alternative built from rows

evals.prompt: Do link building for [XYZ] this month. (Page 00: 'SEO — Active — audit only'. Multi-location, <n> offices.)
evals.expected_output: Scope gate: audit only. Produces the page-level gap, a citation consistency audit against each location's GBP (Windsor, read only) and record rows, a lost-link 301 list for a person to apply, and an unlinked-mention list. States that outreach drafts and new prospect outreach are excluded by the qualifier and offers a scope note. Runs citations per location without mixing name, address or phone. Doesn't edit any listing. Stages OPEN L-row findings as DRAFT in the miner format and lists listing errors as fix-now findings.
assertions: Respects the 'audit only' qualifier and names what it excludes
Writes no outreach drafts
Audits citations against GBP per location without mixing locations
Does not edit GBP or listings
Stages research findings as DRAFT rows and fix-now findings
